title: Introduce profile-merger and unit-econ signature for workload defaults
text:
Introduce profile-merger and unit-econ signature for workload defaults

description:
Problem: we've accumulated multiple overlapping sources of batching/caching/quantization defaults: telemetry-derived suggestions, per-team overrides, and customer-provided profiles. Operators have to reconcile conflicts manually which leads to misconfigurations and avoidable unit-cost regressions.

This PR introduces a lightweight 'profile-merger' service + a deterministic 'unit_econ_signature' that:
- accepts multiple profile inputs (telemetry, team, customer, CLI)
- resolves conflicts with an explainable precedence and confidence score
- emits a canonical merged profile used by runtime and the CLI
- computes a stable signature/hash used by caching, rollout decisions, and cost auditing

Scope of changes (single continuous description string as required): Implements merging logic and precedence rules, CLI to inspect and force-merge profiles, telemetry hooks to tag suggested defaults with confidence windows, unit tests and integration smoke tests, docs for operators, and small runtime switch to use merged profile for batching and quantization presets. No behavioral change to existing defaults until the new merger is enabled through runtime feature flag.

Motivation: reduce manual friction, enable safe automated rollouts of econ defaults, and make decisions auditable for SRE / customer success. Ties into ongoing Econ workstreams to drive platform-wide cost safety.

Checklist:
- [x] Profile-merger core algorithm and API
- [x] CLI 'runit-econ inspect/merge' for operators
- [x] Runtime wiring behind feature flag (off by default)
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Docs and examples

Related: ENG-7123, design note: docs/design/econ/profile-merger.md

review_comments:
Evan Chen: LGTM overall. Please add a short note on how the confidence window decays over time and how telemetry updates are throttled.
Author (Anjali): added 'confidence_decay' config and throttling to telemetry ingestion; updated tests to cover decay behavior.
Marco Varela: Can the signature be stable across process restarts? Need determinism for cache keys.
Author (Anjali): signature is deterministic (stable ordering + canonical serialization). Added unit test asserting stable hash across runs and documented versioning strategy.
Priya Desai: Add a safety gate: when merged profile increases predicted cost by >10% vs baseline, require operator confirmation for rollout.
Author (Anjali): added 'cost_delta_threshold' check and CLI prompt; default threshold 15% (configurable).

release_notes:
- Introduce profile-merger service to deterministically combine telemetry, team, and customer econ profiles.
- Add 'unit_econ_signature' used for caching and audit traces.
- New CLI 'runit-econ' to inspect and force merges.
- Runtime integration behind feature flag (off by default). Operators can enable after validation.

notes_for_ops:
Enable the feature flag 'econ.profile_merger.enabled' in staging for two weeks and observe 'econ_signature_mismatch' alerts. If cost delta alerts fire, use 'runit-econ inspect' to compare contributors and run 'runit-econ merge --confirm' only after operator review.

impact_summary:
Low-risk: runtime change is behind feature flag. Enables future automated rollouts. Adds observability metrics and a small CLI surface for operators.

qa_summary:
Added unit tests covering deterministic signature generation, merge precedence cases, and cost-delta gating. Integration test simulates telemetry + team override + customer profile and verifies merged output and metric emission.

example_usage:
# view merged profile for model: runit-econ inspect --model gpt-small --env staging
# force merge and print signature: runit-econ merge --model gpt-small --source telemetry,team --confirm

follow_up:
1) telemetry service: tag suggestions with longer-term decay window and sample weights (ENG-7180). 2) Integrate merged signatures in the rollout controller to prevent simultaneous incompatible rollouts (ENG-7199).
